channels.name: code-review
channels.topic: Post a PR here to get eyes on it. Say which subsystem it touches and whether it's blocking a release.

messages.text: PR 493 is ready for another look, revamp to the CLI progress bar UI, touches progress-and-cli only and not blocking a release but it's been sitting a while.
what changed from the last version? I want to make sure I'm looking at the right parts.

Main change is the render logic, the old version just did a flat bar, now it layers in per-row status. So the part to look at is the update call:

```python
# before
bar.update(1)

# after
bar.update(1, status=row_status, label=f"{completed}/{total}")
```

rest is mostly wiring that through the callers.
erm, is it just me or is this friday morning moving at half speed, I've read the same paragraph three times already.
so the `row_status` coming in there, is that already resolved to a string or still a raw enum?
already resolved to a string before it gets to the bar, the enum conversion happens upstream of the display layer.
Might be worth having at least one test that passes a bad string through that path
yeah ok, I'll add that.
@Nikolai, where does PR 495 stand

PR 495 is ready for review, teh enhancements and tests are all done, it just needs eyes on it. Also, while people are looking, PR 502 is a telemetry config change that's similarly ready and I'd like to land it today if someone can spare a look.

PR 468 is also sitting out there and I want to make sure it doesn't get lost. It's blocked on issue 52 (multiple samples per request) being settled, so until that's decided it can't really move forward.
Good to have PR 468 confirmed as blocked on issue 52 rather than just floating, at least we know exactly what it's waiting on now.

messages.text: Cost estimation bug is up as PR 504, touches online-request-processing, want to figure out if that's a release blocker or we kick it to v0.1.19.
Did the batch client refactor end up covering all provider paths, or are there gaps still?
multimodal path is showing unexpected behavior since the refactor, image inputs are not processing same way as before
Is it all image inputs or specific formats?
I've been cross-referencing the anthropic vision docs on image content block types, there's more variation in what gets accepted than I expected

Separate thing I want to settle before end of day: when we skip a pending batch job on resume, can we log the reason at INFO, not just the id at DEBUG? "resumed 1 pending batch job" with nothing explaining what didn't match is how I lost an afternoon last month.
Fair point, that's a frustrating way to lose time.
Are they failing outright or just behaving differently?
Honestly I'm not sure this is actually a refactor regression, the batch client changes didn't go near the multimodal path.
From my side the batch client refactor looks solid across the provider paths I've tested
Has anyone actually seen a failure on a specific backend, or are we good to call it stable?
I haven't verified the multimodal path since the refactor
@Dario, can we do a quick sync this afternoon on it
@Dario, where does PR 504 stand, is the cost bug scoped to online-request-processing only?
@Emil that's my PR actually, not Dario's. And I said it looks isolated to online-request-processing but I haven't ruled out the batch path, I haven't dug into it fully
You planning to check the batch path before we classify it, or is that after the fact?
I can't check the batch path without Emil's help, I don't own that side
@Emil, is that something you can pair on this afternoon?
@Dermot, still good for that sync this afternoon, whenever works for you
Yeah
I can do that. Is this a quick look or are you expecting we need a couple hours?
The cost bug in PR 504 is in my code, and from what I can reproduce it's staying in online-request-processing, not hitting the batch path.
Nice, that narrows it down a lot.
@Dario since it's yours, can you take the fix and say whether it blocks release or goes to v0.1.19?
Yeah, I'll look at it now and report back before end of day.
Went through the batch path with Gideon earlier, nothing in there is touched by the cost bug. Refactor looks solid on that side too.
batch path clean and providers stable, solid end to the week
@Emil, can you give the multimodal path a look monday, I wasn't able to confirm it's clean today
Glad it's Friday, this week felt about twice as long as it actually was
calling it for the weekend, back monday
@Dario still waiting on the classification for PR 504, do we have enough to call it before the weekend or is that slipping to Monday?
Looked at PR 504, the bug is isolated and not touching any critical path
Also on the resume skip logging Gideon flagged earlier, that sits in caching-and-resume so I'll pick that up, noting the reason at INFO rather than just the job id at DEBUG

messages.text:
- bulk-llm-inference is stable from my end, no provider path failures in the overnight logs
- multimodal side looks clean, batch submissions coming through normally, nothing flagged
caching-and-resume looks stable on my end too
PR 504 is up for the cost estimation bug, that's what I want to get eyes on today
is the cost bug in PR 504 isolated to online-request-processing, or does it affect the batch path too
From what I can see it's in online-request-processing, I haven't traced it into the batch path but Emil would know better on that side
did the vllm offline test fix get proper coverage, or is it still at risk of slipping
hmm

what's missing from the test coverage on the vllm fix
I'd like that sorted this afternoon, not left for next week
local-offline-inference hardcodes its own model name list, that's what told a vllm user their model can't do schema-constrained output when the same model works fine over the api
I've found three files now carrying the same model strings independently, that list should not be duplicated across the codebase

The hardcoded model list in local-offline-inference is what's blocking me from calling the offline path fully confirmed
is the hardcoded list in local-offline-inference the same one that's in the other two files, or are they actually diverged?

Still want to confirm the cost bug in PR 504 is isolated before we call it done
Around this afternoon if anyone wants to dig into PR 504 scope together
seven provider integrations clean is solid, Dario.
not sure
I haven't done a direct comparison
